neighbours.label: the particle completing a fixed verb-particle phrase, mainly ' in' after engage (engage in), also ' out' in 'mete out'
fire: Both parties agreed to engage in direct talks next month.
Teenagers who engage in sports often sleep better.
The rebels have engaged in sporadic fighting near the border.
Employees must never engage in insider trading.
He likes to engage in long philosophical arguments over dinner.
Researchers asked volunteers to engage in a simple memory task.
Courts were slow to mete out justice to the rioters.
The two firms are engaging in a fierce price war.
quiet: Both parties agreed to take part in direct talks next month.
Teenagers who participate in sports often sleep better.
The rebels have been fighting sporadically in the hills near the border.
Employees must never get mixed up with insider trading.
He likes to engage with his guests over dinner.
Researchers asked volunteers to complete a simple memory task.
Courts were slow to hand down sentences to the rioters.
The two firms are locked in a fierce price war.

notes: Probe: engage(d) in 0.757/0.714/0.828, mete out 0.774; participated in 0.136, engaged with 0.106, engaged to 0.028, lives in 0.005. So not 'in' in general and not participation verbs in general.
